faqs.question: What is a digital gift in simple words?
faqs.answer: It is a gift that arrives as a file, a code or a link rather than a parcel. The four common kinds are gift cards, subscriptions, downloadable files and personalised web pages built for one named person.

faqs.question: Is a digital gift the same as an e-gift card?
faqs.answer: No. An e-gift card is one kind of digital gift — a prepaid code carrying spendable money. Subscriptions, downloads and personalised pages are digital gifts too, and none of them carries redeemable value.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a digital gift and a virtual gift?
faqs.answer: "Virtual gift" usually means a token bought inside a platform, like a rose on a livestream or a sticker in a chat. "Digital gift" is the umbrella term that covers virtual gifts, e-gift cards, subscriptions, downloads and personalised pages.

faqs.question: Do digital gift cards expire in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Reserve Bank of India's Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments, dated 27 August 2021, requires a minimum validity of one year from the date of last loading, and the issuer must warn the holder during the 45 days before it lapses.

faqs.question: How much money can an Indian gift card hold?
faqs.answer: A Gift PPI is capped at ₹10,000 under the RBI Master Direction, and it cannot be reloaded. Cash-out is not permitted either; the balance can only be returned to the account it was loaded from, with the holder's consent.

faqs.question: What is a digital gift website?
faqs.answer: It is a site that builds the gift itself rather than selling a voucher — you add names, photos and text, and it produces a page you send as a link. SubhSandesh is one; 4,357 pages have been built on it since 12 March 2026, across 16 page types.

faqs.question: Are digital gifts actually opened, or do they get ignored?
faqs.answer: It depends on the family. Our 4,357 personalised pages have drawn 49,968 recorded views, an average of 11.5 per page, while Bankrate's September 2024 survey found 43% of US adults holding at least one gift card they had never used.

faqs.question: Can I make a digital gift private?
faqs.answer: On a personalised page, yes — you can set a password before sharing the link, and 40.6% of our creators do exactly that. Gift cards and virtual stickers have no equivalent, because they are designed to be spent rather than read.

faqs.question: How long does it take to make a personalised digital gift?
faqs.answer: Longer than buying a voucher, and that is the point. The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit on our "I love you" template is 6.2 hours, sampled across 1,125 pages — most people come back to it more than once.

faqs.question: Is a digital gift a lazy gift?
faqs.answer: A gift card can be, and Bankrate's data on unused balances suggests recipients sometimes read it that way. A page written about one person is the opposite problem — it takes hours and cannot be regifted, which is why 94.1% of the ones started here get finished and shared.

faqs.question: When should I send something physical instead?
faqs.answer: If the person is in the same room, buy the object; a link is a poor substitute for handing something over. If they do not use a smartphone comfortably, none of the four families works well — 49.0% of our shared pages are opened on a phone.

faqs.question: Do digital gifts work for festivals and weddings?
faqs.answer: They can, but that is not what the category is mostly used for. Occasion-dated pages, every festival and wedding type combined, are only 3.7% of the 4,357 pages built here; the remaining 96.3% are romantic and everyday.

article.contentMarkdown:
# What Is a Digital Gift? The Four Kinds, and Which to Send

A digital gift is anything you give that arrives as a file, a code or a link instead of a parcel — a gift card, a subscription, a downloadable file, or a personalised web page built for one person. Those four families behave completely differently, and only the last one is meant to be looked at rather than spent. We build that last kind, and our own numbers say people treat it like an object: 40.6% of creators password-protect the page before they share it (1,767 of 4,357, measured 2026-09-15), and the median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.2 hours, sampled across 1,125 "I love you" pages. Nobody fusses over a voucher for six hours. This page defines each family, compares them on delivery and expiry, and says plainly which one fits which situation.

## What is a digital gift?

A digital gift is a gift whose whole substance is data: it is delivered over the internet, it has no physical form, and the recipient opens it on a screen. The physical object is replaced either by spendable value, by access to something, by a file, or by an experience made for one named person.

That definition is wider than the one most pages use. Search "digital gift" today and nearly every result explains gift cards, because gift cards are the part of the category with a payments industry attached to it. India's gift card and incentive card market was worth about US$8.96 billion in 2024 and is [forecast to reach roughly US$18.03 billion by 2029](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/03/06/3038274/0/en/India-Gift-Card-and-Incentive-Card-Databook-Report-2025-An-18-Billion-Industry-by-2029-Market-Intelligence-and-Future-Growth-Dynamics-2020-2029.html), according to a Research and Markets databook published in March 2025.

But a Spotify subscription, a Kindle book pushed to someone's account, a Procreate brush pack and a page that plays your voice are all digital gifts too. None is a gift card.

## Digital gift, virtual gift, e-gift card — are these the same thing?

No, and the difference matters when you are choosing. "E-gift card" is the narrowest term: a prepaid code redeemable at one brand or across a card network. "Virtual gift" usually means a token bought inside a platform — a rose on a livestream, a sticker in a chat. "Digital gift" is the umbrella covering all of it, including things that carry no monetary value at all.

In India the e-gift card corner of the category is regulated. Under the Reserve Bank of India's [Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12156), dated 27 August 2021, a Gift PPI may not exceed ₹10,000, may not be reloaded, and permits no cash-out — funds can only go back to the source account, with the holder's consent. Every PPI must carry a minimum validity of one year from the date of last loading, and the issuer must warn the holder during the 45 days before it lapses.

Nothing in that paragraph applies to a subscription, a download or a personalised page. Those are the three families people forget they have.

## The four families of digital gift

### 1. Stored value: gift cards, vouchers and prepaid codes

What it is: a code carrying spendable money, redeemable at one brand or anywhere a card network is accepted. Who it suits: someone whose taste you genuinely do not know, or a group gift where cash would be awkward. What it costs: whatever you load, capped at ₹10,000 per Gift PPI in India. What happens next: it gets spent, or it does not — Bankrate's 2024 survey of 2,373 US adults found [43% were holding at least one unused gift card](https://www.bankrate.com/credit-cards/news/gift-cards-survey/), averaging US$244 each.

### 2. Access: subscriptions, memberships and passes

What it is: a paid term on something the recipient uses repeatedly — music, video, a newspaper, a gym, a course. Who it suits: someone with an established habit you can subsidise. What it costs: one term up front, with renewal falling to them afterwards. What happens next: the best-case outcome is that they forget it was a gift, because it has become part of their week. The worst case is an auto-renew charge they did not plan for.

### 3. Digital goods: downloads, files and licences

What it is: a file that becomes theirs permanently — an ebook, an album, a font, a plugin, a photo book PDF. Who it suits: hobbyists and anyone with a specific tool they have mentioned wanting. What it costs: a one-off price, usually smaller than a comparable physical object. What happens next: nothing is observable. Once the file is downloaded, the giver learns nothing about whether it was opened.

### 4. Personalised pages: a page built for one named person

What it is: a web page made about a specific person — their name, your photos, your writing — sent as a link that opens in a browser with nothing to install. Who it suits: someone who already has everything, or is 2,000 km away at 11pm. What it costs: time more than money; our median build runs 6.2 hours from first save to last edit. What happens next: it is read, reread and kept. Our 4,357 pages have drawn 49,968 recorded views, an average of 11.5 per page.

## Compare the four on delivery, expiry and what can be measured

The four families differ most on two things nobody puts in a listicle: what the Indian rulebook says about expiry, and how much the giver ever gets to find out.

| Family | Reaches them in | Expiry under Indian rules | What can actually be measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stored value | Seconds, by email or SMS | Minimum 1 year from last loading (RBI, 2021) | 43% of US adults hold an unused card, US$244 average (Bankrate, Sept 2024) |
| Access | Minutes, as a redeemable code | Ends with the paid term | Renewal decisions pass to the recipient after term one |
| Digital goods | Seconds, as a file or link | Never — the file is theirs | Nothing after the download completes |
| Personalised page | Seconds, as a link | Never — the page stays live | 4,357 pages, 49,968 views, 11.5 views per page, 40.6% password-protected (SubhSandesh, 2026-09-15) |

The takeaway: stored value is the easiest to send and the easiest to waste, and a personalised page is the only family where the giver sees the gift being returned to.

## Where personalised pages sit, and what people actually do with them

This family is the newest and the least documented — search "digital gift website" and you mostly get voucher marketplaces — so here is what our own database says. Of 4,357 pages built since 12 March 2026 across 16 page types, 94.1% were actually published and shared — 4,098 of them. That is an unusually low abandonment rate for anything people build from a blank page, and the clearest signal we have that the format is not fiddly.

The most-built page is a straightforward [romantic "I love you" page](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf) at 1,125 pages, 25.8% of everything created. Second is a [hand-tied digital bouquet](https://subhsandesh.in/bouquet-gf) at 1,070 pages, 24.6% — flowers, minus the florist and the delivery window. Neither is a festival page. Occasion-dated pages, every festival and wedding type combined, are only 3.7% of what gets built; this is a 96.3% everyday category.

Two behaviours are worth knowing before you build one. 49.0% of shared pages are opened on a phone, so a wide desktop layout is being read on a 6-inch screen. And 40.6% of creators set a password first — a digital gift is often meant for exactly one pair of eyes, which is the opposite of how vouchers and virtual stickers work. If you want to see the range before committing, the [full template list](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) is the place to start.

## What research says about sending a gift as a link

The academic work here is thin, but two studies are directly on point. Hyosun Kwon's 2022 study in Archives of Design Research, [Exploring Digital Gifting Rituals](https://aodr.org/xml/33129/33129.pdf), used diary probes and follow-up interviews and concluded that digital gifting "lacks the common vocabulary of exchange rituals" — there is no digital equivalent of wrapping paper, of handing something over, of watching a face change. Her design recommendations are about restoring exactly that: keeping the momentum of the ritual, synchronising giving and receiving, and building a mutual bond.

The second is a May 2023 paper in Psychology & Marketing, [Gifting digital versus physical gift cards](https://doi.org/10.1002/mar.21790) by Reshadi, Givi and Das. Across five studies they found the hesitation sits with the giver, not the recipient: givers are less likely to choose a digital gift card than recipients are to prefer receiving one, partly because givers overestimate how much a digital gift reads as a breach of gift-giving norms. Only the abstract is readable without a subscription, and nothing beyond it is claimed here.

Both point the same way. The awkwardness of a digital gift is mostly the sender's, and what dissolves it is making the arrival feel like an event — which is why six hours spent editing a page are not wasted.

## When a digital gift is the wrong choice

If the person is in the same room, buy the thing. A link is a poor substitute for handing something over — Kwon's research is an account of exactly what gets lost when you remove that moment.

If the recipient does not use a smartphone comfortably, none of these four families works well — and with 49.0% of our pages opened on a phone, a parent who reads on a shared family tablet is a genuinely worse fit. If what is wanted is money with no strings, a UPI transfer is more honest than a voucher capped at ₹10,000 that cannot be cashed out.

And if the occasion is an obligation rather than a relationship — a colleague's farewell, a client's Diwali — a gift card is the correct, unsentimental answer. A personalised page for someone you barely know is worse than no gift at all. Note too that the Bankrate survey above is US data; we found no equivalent India-wide measurement of unused gift card balances.

## Sources

- [Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs)](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12156) — Reserve Bank of India, 27 August 2021
- [Survey: 43% of Americans have at least one unused gift card](https://www.bankrate.com/credit-cards/news/gift-cards-survey/) — Bankrate / YouGov, 20 September 2024, n = 2,373 US adults
- [India Gift Card and Incentive Card Databook Report 2025](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/03/06/3038274/0/en/India-Gift-Card-and-Incentive-Card-Databook-Report-2025-An-18-Billion-Industry-by-2029-Market-Intelligence-and-Future-Growth-Dynamics-2020-2029.html) — Research and Markets, 6 March 2025
- [Exploring Digital Gifting Rituals](https://aodr.org/xml/33129/33129.pdf) — Hyosun Kwon, Archives of Design Research 35(2), May 2022
- [Gifting digital versus physical gift cards](https://doi.org/10.1002/mar.21790) — Reshadi, Givi and Das, Psychology & Marketing, May 2023 (abstract only)

auditReport.honestAssessment: Every page ranking for this query — including the two India-specific ones — treats "digital gift" as a synonym for "digital gift card" and writes for a merchant or an HR buyer. This is the only page that splits the category into four families and the only one that can put measured behaviour behind the newest family: 4,357 pages, a 6.2-hour median build, 40.6% password-protected, 94.1% finished. Two weaknesses are real — the unused-gift-card figure is US data with no Indian equivalent found, the Psychology & Marketing paper is paywalled so only its abstract was read, and the domain is far below Razorpay's or Blackhawk's authority, so any movement here takes months and depends on links this post cannot generate on its own.
